process_area.title: Pro-Referral Matchmaking, Project Routing & Lead Management

fields.Owner: CX (VS-13) / Pro-Referral Network Manager / Store Ops
fields.Participants: CX (VS-13), Store Ops (VS-07), Digital (VS-10/VS-75), Privacy/DPO (VS-91), Marketplace (VS-95)

Automation Opportunity: - Request-intake forms (online/app); consent capture; qualification rules; auto-route to matchmaking
Controls: - CTL-747 (ensure controlled execution — Pro-Referral Matchmaking, Project Routing & Lead Management (PA-172.2).)
- CTL-747: consent captured (VS-91); disclaimer set; request qualified; routed to matchmaking
Cross-references: - links to VS-91 (privacy/consent), VS-10/VS-75 (digital), VS-95 (marketplace), VS-13 (CX), W4991 (demand), W4994 (matchmaking), W4995 (handoff)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Privacy risk**: Sharing customer data without consent (RA 10173); mitigated by consent capture
- **Mis-expectation risk**: Customer expecting BuildRight guarantees/employment; mitigated by clear disclaimer
- **Lead-quality risk**: Vague/invalid requests waste installer time; mitigated by qualification

steps.activity: Intake the request: capture the customer's project need (trade/specialty, scope, location, timing, budget), the linked materials/order (links VS-10/VS-11) where applicable, and contact details; qualify the request (real intent, scope clarity)

Capture consent & set expectations: capture consent to share contact/project details with installers (RA 10173 — links VS-91), set expectations (response time, referral-not-guarantee disclaimer, that the installer is an independent contractor not BuildRight's employee), and confirm the referral terms
Route to matchmaking: qualify-and-route the request to matchmaking (W4994), manage incomplete/invalid requests, and feed demand analytics (W4991)

Automation Opportunity: - Matchmaking engine (trade/area/capacity/rating); routing-rule engine; acceptance tracking; load-balance alerts
Controls: - CTL-747 (ensure controlled execution — Pro-Referral Matchmaking, Project Routing & Lead Management (PA-172.2).)
- CTL-747: match criteria accurate; routing fair; lead-acceptance tracked; unaccepted escalated (W5000)
Cross-references: - links to VS-95 (marketplace), VS-29 (location), VS-129 (fairness), W4989 (tier), W4993 (intake), W4995 (handoff), W4999 (capacity), W5000 (recovery), W5003 (rating)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-match risk**: Wrong trade/area/capacity → poor outcome; mitigated by accurate matching criteria
- **Routing-fairness risk**: Unfair routing favoring some installers (VS-129); mitigated by fair/rotational rules
- **Unaccepted-lead risk**: Installer declines/ignores → unfulfilled referral; mitigated by W5000 recovery
System Touchpoints: - Marketplace/matchmaking (VS-95); CRM/lead (VS-11/VS-107); location master (VS-29); analytics (VS-28); privacy (VS-91)

steps.activity: Match the request to installers: by trade specialty, service area/location (links VS-29), capacity/availability (W4999), tier (preferred-first W4989), rating (W5003), and pricing fit; produce a ranked shortlist

Distribute the lead: route the lead to the matched installer(s) per the routing model (preferred-first, rotation, or broadcast-auction), with the customer/project details (per consent W4993), and track acceptance/decline
Manage routing rules & fairness: tune the routing model for fairness/anti-discrimination (links VS-129), monitor fill-rate and installer-load balance (W4999), and escalate unaccepted leads (W5000)

fields.Participants: Installer, CX (VS-13), Marketplace (VS-95), Sales Enablement (VS-124), Privacy (VS-91)

workflows.name: Lead Handoff, Customer-Installer Communication & Quote Management

Automation Opportunity: - Platform-masked comms; quote capture/template; SLA tracking; pricing-fairness alerts
Controls: - CTL-747 (ensure controlled execution — Pro-Referral Matchmaking, Project Routing & Lead Management (PA-172.2).)
- CTL-747: handoff confirmed; quote captured; pricing fair (VS-129); comms governed; privacy respected
Cross-references: - links to VS-95 (marketplace), VS-12/VS-11 (pricing), VS-129 (competition), VS-91 (privacy), VS-13 (CX), W4994 (routing), W4996 (booking)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-show risk**: Installer doesn't follow up → customer disappointment; mitigated by SLA and W5000
- **Quote-fairness risk**: Predatory/over-pricing (VS-129); mitigated by pricing governance
- **Communication-failure risk**: Poor customer↔installer comms → disputes; mitigated by platform comms and CX support

steps.activity: Hand off & connect: provide the installer the customer/project details (per consent W4993), connect customer↔installer (via platform-masked comms or direct per consent), and confirm the installer's acknowledgement and site-visit/quote timing

Manage the quote: the installer provides a quote/proposal (scope, price, timeline, materials), the customer reviews/negotiates/accepts, and the platform captures the quote for transparency (links VS-12/VS-11 pricing)

Support & govern: CX supports the customer through the quote, govern pricing fairness (VS-129 anti-predatory), manage communication/complaints (VS-13), and capture consent/privacy on the ongoing exchange

fields.Participants: Installer, CX (VS-13), Sales/Store Ops (VS-07/VS-11), Ecommerce (VS-10), Finance (VS-154)

workflows.name: Project Booking, Scope Confirmation & Materials-Link Sales Attach

Automation Opportunity: - Booking-from-quote; materials-link/attach recommendations; financing/warranty offers; milestone/payment setup
Controls: - CTL-747 (ensure controlled execution — Pro-Referral Matchmaking, Project Routing & Lead Management (PA-172.2).)
- CTL-747: scope documented & confirmed; materials linked; booking captured; tracking set up
Cross-references: - links to VS-10/VS-11/VS-16 (order/materials), VS-154 (financing), VS-53 (warranty), VS-66 (design), W4995 (quote), W4997 (settlement), W4998 (tracking), W5001 (rating)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scope-creep risk**: Unclear scope → disputes/overruns; mitigated by documented scope
- **Attach-miss risk**: Materials attach not captured → lost BuildRight sales; mitigated by materials-link
- **Booking-error risk**: Wrong schedule/scope; mitigated by confirmation controls
System Touchpoints: - Marketplace/CRM (VS-95/VS-11); ecommerce/order (VS-10/VS-16); financing (VS-154); warranty (VS-53); finance (VS-17/VS-16); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Book the project: confirm the scope/price/timeline/materials, schedule the work (links W4998 execution), capture the booking in the platform/CRM, and confirm with the customer and installer

Confirm materials & sales attach: confirm/link the materials (BuildRight SKUs — links VS-10/VS-11 order), drive materials attach (additional SKUs the project needs), and offer financing (VS-154) / warranty (VS-53) / design (VS-66) where relevant
Document & set up tracking: document the project scope/booking, set the milestone/payment plan (W4997/W4998), and establish the project-execution tracking (W4998) and rating/feedback cycle (W5001)

fields.Volume: ~300–600 settlements per month (per completed project) × network

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-compute fee on completion; marketplace settlement; BIR-compliant invoicing; revenue-assurance alerts
Controls: - CTL-747: economics defined; fee captured at completion; BIR-compliant; reconciled; audited (VS-21)
Cross-references: - links to VS-17/VS-16 (finance), VS-79 (tax/BIR), VS-118 (revenue assurance), VS-21 (audit), VS-11 (B2B), W4985 (strategy), W4996 (booking), W4998 (completion)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Revenue-leakage risk**: Fees not collected (VS-118); mitigated by capture-at-completion and reconciliation
- **Tax-compliance risk**: VAT/EWT on installer fees mis-handled (VS-79); mitigated by BIR-compliant billing
- **Dispute risk**: Installer disputes fees; mitigated by clear terms and audit trail
System Touchpoints: - Finance/AP-AR (VS-17/VS-16); marketplace settlement (VS-95); tax/BIR (VS-79); revenue assurance (VS-118); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Define the referral economics: the referral-fee/commission model (flat per lead, % of project value, % of materials sold, or marketplace transaction fee), the free-vs-charge thresholds, the B2B/contract treatment (VS-11), and the tax (BIR VAT/EWT on installer fees links VS-79)

Calculate & settle: compute the referral fee/commission per completed project (W4998), invoice/collect from the installer (or deduct from marketplace settlement), issue BIR-compliant billing (links VS-79), and reconcile to finance (VS-17/VS-16)
Govern & audit: monitor fee leakage/revenue assurance (links VS-118), disputes/installer pushback, audit the settlement (VS-21), and refine the economics (W4985)

workflows.name: Project Execution Tracking, Milestone & Completion Verification

Automation Opportunity: - Milestone tracking; completion-verification workflow; delay alerts; rating trigger on completion
Controls: - CTL-747: milestones tracked; completion verified; exceptions escalated; scorecard updated (W5003)
Cross-references: - links to VS-12 (dispatch comparison), VS-13 (CX), VS-53 (warranty), VS-95 (marketplace), W4996 (booking), W4997 (settlement), W5001 (rating), W5003 (scorecard), W5005 (disputes)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Delay/abandonment risk**: Installer delays/abandons → customer harm; mitigated by tracking and W5000/W5005
- **Completion-dispute risk**: Customer disputes completion/quality; mitigated by verification and W5005
- **Tracking-blindness risk**: No visibility into active projects; mitigated by platform tracking
System Touchpoints: - Marketplace/project tracking (VS-95); CRM (VS-11); CX (VS-13); warranty (VS-53); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Track execution & milestones: the installer reports progress/milestones (start, materials, phase completion), the platform tracks status, and CX monitors for delays/issues (links VS-12 dispatch for own-crew comparison)
Verify completion: on claimed completion, verify the work (customer confirmation, photo evidence, scope check), confirm milestone payments (W4997), and trigger the rating/feedback cycle (W5001)
Manage exceptions: delays, scope disputes, quality issues, abandonment — escalate to dispute resolution (W5005), offer alternate installers (W5000), and document for the scorecard (W5003)

Automation Opportunity: - Capacity/calendar auto-sync; workload-balance routing; overload alerts; capacity-gap forecasting
Controls: - CTL-747 (ensure controlled execution — Pro-Referral Matchmaking, Project Routing & Lead Management (PA-172.2).)
- CTL-747: capacity/calendar current; workload balanced; capacity gaps managed; fairness maintained (VS-129)
Cross-references: - links to VS-95 (marketplace), VS-129 (fairness), VS-64/VS-69 (peaks), VS-12/VS-06/VS-143 (alternatives), W4991 (gaps), W4994 (routing)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Overload risk**: Preferred installer over-booked → delays; mitigated by workload balancing
- **Capacity-constraint risk**: Insufficient capacity at peaks; mitigated by surge/recruitment
- **Stale-calendar risk**: Out-of-date availability → mis-routing; mitigated by freshness controls

steps.activity: Maintain installer capacity & calendar: per-installer availability, capacity (jobs/week), service area, and blackout/unavailability; keep current for matchmaking (W4994)
Balance workload: avoid overloading preferred installers (which delays response/completion), distribute leads fairly (links VS-129 fairness), and route to available capacity (W4994)
Manage capacity gaps: when capacity is constrained (peak season VS-64, disaster recovery VS-69), recruit/surge (W4986/W4991) or recommend BuildRight's own crews (VS-12)/delivery (VS-06/VS-143)

fields.Trigger: Lead declined/unaccepted (W4994); quote lost (W4995); installer unavailable
fields.Volume: ~500–1,000 lost/declined leads per month across the network

workflows.name: Lost/Declined Lead Recovery, Alternate Referral & Demand Capture

Automation Opportunity: - Lost-lead auto-flag; auto-re-route; alternate-offer automation; loss-reason analytics
Controls: - CTL-747 (ensure controlled execution — Pro-Referral Matchmaking, Project Routing & Lead Management (PA-172.2).)
- CTL-747: lost leads detected within SLA; alternate referral offered; demand captured; loss reasons analyzed
Cross-references: - links to VS-95 (marketplace), VS-12 (own crews), VS-06/VS-143 (alternatives), VS-154 (financing), VS-66 (design), W4991 (coverage), W4994 (routing), W4995 (quote)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lost-referral risk**: Unfulfilled referral → lost attach/CLV; mitigated by recovery
- **Customer-churn risk**: Customer leaves for a competitor; mitigated by fast alternate referral
- **Demand-blindness risk**: Lost demand not captured/learned; mitigated by demand capture & analytics

steps.activity: Detect lost/declined leads: monitor unaccepted leads (W4994), lost quotes (W4995), and abandoned requests; flag for recovery within the response SLA

Recover via alternate referral: re-route to alternate installers (W4994), offer BuildRight's own crews (VS-12) where available, or recommend delivery/alternatives (VS-06/VS-143); keep the customer engaged

Capture demand & learn: even if referral fails, capture the project demand (materials sale, financing VS-154, design VS-66), analyze loss reasons (coverage W4991, pricing, capacity), and feed improvement
